title: AI-Generated Hot Girls Are Ripping Off Comedians to Boost Their Horny Content
key_facts: WIRED identified eight comics whose videos were replicated by scantily clad, AI-generated women, many following each other on social media.
Comedian Julia Jasunas found her joke repeated word for word by an account called Aylen Skye (250,000 Instagram followers), which links to adult content on the subscription site Fanvue.
Meta told Jasunas the video did not violate community guidelines because the account was not pretending to be her.
Instagram's rules prohibit impersonation but not copying content that is not copyrighted, and allow AI content if it is labelled; some accounts are labelled and others are not.

Comedian George Brett Olson posted a viral comparison on 3 Oct of his joke and a near-identical one by an account called Tiffany Sloane (about 375,000 followers); Sloane commented 'sorry, won't happen again' and deleted its video.
Instagram head Adam Mosseri said it was not 'practical for us to try and ban AI content' but the platform was 'very invested in trying to drive more traffic to original content creators'.
Jokes have historically had little copyright protection, and an intellectual property lawyer told Olson a lawsuit was probably more trouble than it was worth.
All the AI accounts flagged by WIRED were still on the platform.
quote_evidence: WIRED has identified eight comics whose videos have been replicated by scantily clad, AI-generated women, many of whom follow each other on social media.
Though Instagram’s community guidelines prohibit impersonation, such policies don’t extend to copying someone else’s content, particularly if that content isn’t copyrighted.
All of the AI-generated accounts flagged by WIRED are still on the platform.
why_it_matters_hint: AI-made influencer accounts are copying comedians' work and platform rules do not clearly stop it.
event_date: WIRED report 16 Oct 2026; Olson's viral post 3 Oct 2026
notes: Single-outlet investigation; the accused accounts did not comment.
